failureMessage: A conflict marker left behind breaks the file, and in a rules or config file it silently changes what the repo instructs every later session and check to do.

matchLines.what: a merge-conflict marker line survives here
matchLines.fix: Finish the resolution, delete the marker line, then re-read the whole file before staging — never chain the grep that checks for markers with the command that stages.

failureMessage: the repo root holds the vendored canon and every pack, so a widened assets directory publishes the agent tooling to claudinite.com

requirePaths.what: wrangler.json is gone, so nothing declares what the release uploads
requirePaths.fix: restore wrangler.json — the release reads its assets.directory and its custom-domain routes, and without it `wrangler deploy` has no target at all

checkParsedFiles.fix: set assets.directory to "./site" — the one published tree; widening it publishes the vendored mount and the packs beside it

checkParsedFiles.what: wrangler.json names a Worker script entry point
checkParsedFiles.fix: drop "main" — claudinite.com is static assets only, and site/privacy.html tells visitors there is no server of ours behind the page; adding one changes that promise and its disclosure first
pin compatibility_date, so the runtime a release lands on is a value in the repo rather than whatever the deploy day defaults to

failureMessage: a workflow that publishes ships the site with no version cut, no gate and no park lane — and a green run looks exactly like success

matchLines.what: {match} publishes the site from a workflow
matchLines.fix: publish from the site-release task's worker instead — `wrangler` is a CLI, so the release needs no `uses:` step

failureMessage: the executor hands code-work only the secrets a task names, so an undeclared one can never arrive and the run fails inside wrangler instead of parking

checkParsedFiles.fix: list CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN in code_work_required_secrets — the executor hands a task only the secrets it names, and parks naming the one a repo has not configured
list CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID in code_work_required_secrets — wrangler needs the account as much as the token, and an unset one fails mid-upload rather than at the gate
declare on_interrupt: "needs-human" — publishing is a one-shot external effect, so a recovery path that re-executes the run must converge to triage instead

failureMessage: a committed token beacons from every checkout and a rewritten placeholder stops counting visits — and neither makes the page look wrong

checkEachFile.fix: restore the placeholder as the token's only value in the committed file — the release substitutes it at upload time, and the token is never committed

failureMessage: site/README.md tells the next reader how the site reaches production, and a confident description of a flow that no longer exists is worse than none

requireCoChange.what: {path} changes the release contract, and site/README.md did not change with it
requireCoChange.fix: correct the release paragraph in site/README.md in this same commit, or make the change one that leaves the description true
